Maya R: Uploaded checkpoint + tokenizer for quetzal-7b-v2 to s3://redwood-models/incoming/quetzal-7b-v2/ . Manifest signed by Kevin M. Size ~12.3G. Can someone sanity-check checksums and tokenizer?
artifact-bot: New artifact received: quetzal-7b-v2 checkpoint (12.3 GB). Signed-manifest=kevin.m@redwood.com. KMS key=aws-kms-prod-01. Auto-scan queued.
Sam L: Thanks — can you paste the sha256 output from the node that uploaded it? I'll compare with registry ledger.
Maya R: Sure — ran locally after upload:
```
$ sha256sum quetzal-7b-v2.tar.gz
5f2d8a1b3c4e6f7890abcd1234567890abcdef1234567890abcdef123456789a  quetzal-7b-v2.tar.gz
```
Sam L: Registry ledger expected sha256: b7c9d0a1e2f34567890abcdeffedcba09876543211234567890abcdef12345678 — that's different.
Jules P: Looks like a mismatch. Was this a direct partner push or did it pass through our multipart CLI? Different upload flows sometimes change metadata or produce corrupted parts. Any SFTP origin?
Maya R: Partner SFTP -> I then did an AWS multipart upload from our transfer node. MD5 matched the partner's digest but sha256 differs. Also tokenizer.json inside the tar reports vocab_size 50304 while our registry expects 50256.
Kevin M: I did sign the manifest for the original artifact the partner provided. We need chain-of-custody before onboarding. @Anika S can you open a ticket with Security + SRE and include object versions + signer? If upload corrupted we must not register as canonical.
Anika S: Opening ticket INV-2026-014 now and adding S3 object versions, transfer logs, and the signed manifest. Also kicking off a re-download from partner endpoint for verification.
Sam L: Procedural note: until checksums and tokenizer-gate pass, set onboarding_status = "intake-blocked". Also attach a minimal eval plan: perplexity on evalset, generation quality smoke, and single-GPU int8/4bit quant runs.
Maya R: Quick quant plan (sketch): run bitsandbytes int8 and ggml-4bit locally on a single A100; measure token latency @512 context; smoke evals with prompt-suite v3.1. Will push bench config to repo ml-onboard/quetzal/bench.yaml.
Jules P: If tokenizer vocab differs we risk tokenization drift. Run tokenizer-checker to generate token mapping diff; if token-level OOV or mapping changes >0.1% escalate.
artifact-bot: Scan result: md5 matches partner-provided value, sha256 mismatch detected, tokenizer schema mismatch (vocab_size). No malware signatures. Flagged for human review.
Kevin M: OK — once the reupload matches registry sha256 we sign and move artifact to staging bucket, then trigger presubmit evals and quant experiments. Also we must record provenance: object version, signer, KMS key, transfer node IP.
Maya R: Reuploaded new tar (forced multipart retry) at 1918765730 — new S3 object version v3. New sha256 below:
```
$ sha256sum quetzal-7b-v2.tar.gz
b7c9d0a1e2f34567890abcdeffedcba09876543211234567890abcdef12345678  quetzal-7b-v2.tar.gz
```
Sam L: Verified against ledger — matches expected. Moving artifact to s3://redwood-models/staging/quetzal-7b-v2/ and kicking off quant experiments + eval harness. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
Jules P: Reminder: add tokenizer diff report and a short regression checklist (perp delta thresholds, sample outputs) to the onboarding PR so QA can sign off. :eyes:
